records.failureSummary: Ran the full suite and audited AC naming / coverage for slice-2 (FR-7 persistence and data security) without modifying any product code. pnpm test (node --test) exits 0: tests 50, suites 0, pass 50, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, todo 0, duration ~1800 ms. No failures to triage; fixTaskType NONE. [AC-04] naming audit: exactly 25 test case names carry the [AC-04] identifier across test/atomic-write.test.js (6), test/data-dir-persistence.test.js (5), test/persistence/security.test.js (6), test/signing-key-persistence.test.js (4) and src/data-layer.test.js (4); the canonical plaintext-leak guard is named [AC-04][FR-7.3] recursive scan of every file under DATA_DIR finds no occurrence of the plaintext password P. Recursive-coverage verification: that guard uses listFilesRecursively (explicit stack walk that descends every subdirectory and skips symlinks) plus readAllDataFiles (reads every regular file as UTF-8), then filters content.includes(P) and asserts deepEqual(offenders, []), so it scans all files under DATA_DIR rather than only the users file. Red-capability (non-vacuity) verification: the [AC-04] cases statically import src/password-hash.js and src/atomic-store.js, so an absent implementation makes the file error (module not found) and the suite exits non-zero; the assertion is a real predicate, not always-true, so a store that persisted the plaintext would fail it. Demonstrated empirically by the audit probe (node --test qa-ac04-nonvacuity.spec.mjs), which reuses the identical predicate, plants the test plaintext only in a nested file and observes it flagged: 2 passed, 0 failed. Endpoint independence: no test file references /api/ or fetch(, and grep for skip, todo and .only( returned no matches, so no case is masked and none fails because of an unimplemented route. Sensitive-value check: the plaintext fixture occurs only in test source, and the captured stdout plus this summary contain no plaintext password and no signing-key value (only temp paths, uuids and hashes). NOTE / process issue: the engine red-light check runs pnpm test expecting failure and reports VACUOUS_TEST because the slice implementation already exists at audit time while the QA role forbids modifying or reverting product code, so a genuine red-first run cannot be produced from this task; recorded as a HIGH issue with a scheduling recommendation, not a product defect.
